title: A Postcard for the Kitchen
premise: Oscar Almeida has kept his struggling café afloat for twenty years with small, careful steps, sustained by a decade of anonymous letters from a stranger who understood him better than anyone. When Mara Voss—the letter writer—moves in next door fleeing her own ruined career as an investigative journalist, their connection deepens into love just as a predatory developer's fraud threatens to take the café and half the block. Mara must decide whether to resurrect the investigative work that once destroyed her life to expose the scheme, while Oscar must choose between selling out quietly or fighting beside her. They expose the developer at a public hearing days before the last ferry of the season, saving the café not through money but through community—and choosing each other openly.
about_author: Sebastian Blackwood is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing love stories on the backs of order tickets during slow shifts. He now lives in a coastal town where the ferries genuinely do stop running each winter.

chapters.title: The Letters I Never Answered
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Three missed payments from losing the café he rebuilt after catastrophe, Oscar rereads the decade of unsigned letters that kept him steady—then meets Mara Voss moving into the apartment next door, and recognizes her handwriting on a moving box. Emotional beat: guarded hope cracking open old loneliness.

chapters.title: What the Flour Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Oscar and Mara circle each other over borrowed sugar and late-night kitchen talks, neither admitting they know the other's secret. Mara discovers the developer's eviction notices are built on forged loan documents—a story she swore never to chase again after it cost her everything. Emotional beat: intimacy blooming alongside dread.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Timetable
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The developer offers Oscar a buyout that would erase his debt and his history; Mara digs into records and finds witnesses from the neighborhood willing to talk only if she puts her name on the byline again. Oscar, feeling the pull between safety and her, asks her to stop—for them. Emotional beat: love against duty, both hearts breaking honestly.

chapters.title: A Postcard for the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax and resolution. At the zoning hearing, Mara testifies under her own name with the forged documents; the neighbors stand with them, the deal collapses, and the café survives on community goodwill rather than luck. On the pier before the last ferry, Oscar gives Mara a postcard—his first written reply in ten years. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, and two people finally seen.
